citation.title: Sharp bounds on the variance in randomized experiments

standing_assumptions: [Population and design: Section 2, p. 851 (PDF p. 2)] Consider a population $U_N$ consisting of $N \ge 4$ units. From $U_N$, $n$ units are randomly sampled into the experimental sample, and the remaining $N - n$ units are left unsampled. Of the $n$ sampled units, $m \ge 2$ units are randomly assigned to the treatment condition, and $n - m \ge 2$ units are randomly assigned to the control condition. Let the indicator variable $X_i^T$ be one if unit $i$ is assigned to the treatment condition, and let the indicator $X_i^C$ be one if unit $i$ is assigned to the control condition. If $X_i^T = X_i^C = 0$, then the unit is unsampled. Since units are sampled without replacement, $X_i^T + X_i^C \le 1$. Without loss of generality, assume an index ordering $i = 1, \ldots, N$ such that those assigned to treatment come first, $X_1^T, \ldots, X_m^T = 1$, and those assigned to control come after, $X_{m+1}^C, \ldots, X_n^C = 1$, and the remaining $N - n$ unsampled units, if any, come last. Associated with each unit $i$ are two potential outcomes [13, 15] under control and treatment, respectively: $y_{0i}$ and $y_{1i}$. For each unit $i$, the analyst then observes $y_{0i}$ when $X_i^C = 1$ and $y_{1i}$ when $X_i^T = 1$. Given elements $v_i, w_i$ for $i = 1, \ldots, N$, we define the finite population mean $\mu_N(v)$, finite population variance $\sigma_N^2(v)$ and finite population covariance $\sigma_N(v, w)$, respectively, as $\mu_N(v) = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N v_i$, $\sigma_N^2(v) = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\{v_i - \mu_N(v)\}^2$, $\sigma_N(v, w) = \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\{v_i - \mu_N(v)\}\{w_i - \mu_N(w)\}$. The average treatment effect for the population $U_N$ is $\tau_N = \mu_N(y_1) - \mu_N(y_0)$. The difference-in-means estimator of $\tau_N$ is (1) $\hat\tau_N = \hat\mu_N(y_1) - \hat\mu_N(y_0) = \frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m y_{1i} - \frac{1}{n-m}\sum_{i=m+1}^n y_{0i}$, with $\mathrm{E}_X(\hat\tau_N) = \tau_N$, where the expectation operator $\mathrm{E}_X$ averages over all $\binom{N}{n}\binom{n}{m}$ possible treatment assignments. Our inferential target is the variance of $\hat\tau_N$. Adapting Freedman [3], Proposition 1, the variance is (2) $V_N = \frac{1}{N-1}\left\{\frac{N-m}{m}\sigma_N^2(y_1) + \frac{N-(n-m)}{n-m}\sigma_N^2(y_0) + 2\sigma_N(y_1, y_0)\right\}$. [Reading: the potential outcomes are deterministic (p. 850: 'a nonparametric model of deterministic potential outcomes'); the only randomness is the assignment, the $\binom{N}{n}\binom{n}{m}$ assignments being equally likely; $\mathrm{E}_X$, $\mathrm{Var}_X$ and $\mathrm{P}$ refer to it.] [Marginal variance estimators: p. 852 (PDF p. 3)] By Cochran [1], Theorem 2.4, unbiased estimators of $\sigma_N^2(y_1)$ and $\sigma_N^2(y_0)$ are $\hat\sigma_N^2(y_1) = \frac{N-1}{N(m-1)}\sum_{i=1}^m\{y_{1i} - \hat\mu_N(y_1)\}^2$, $\hat\sigma_N^2(y_0) = \frac{N-1}{N(n-m-1)}\sum_{i=m+1}^n\{y_{0i} - \hat\mu_N(y_0)\}^2$. [The case $n = N$: Section 2.1, pp. 852–853 (PDF pp. 3–4)] When $n = N$, the sampling variance of the difference-in-means estimator reduces to (3) $V_n = \frac{1}{n-1}\left\{\frac{n-m}{m}\sigma_n^2(y_1) + \frac{m}{n-m}\sigma_n^2(y_0) + 2\sigma_n(y_1, y_0)\right\}$. (4) $\hat V_n^a = \frac{n}{n-1}\left\{\frac{\hat\sigma_n^2(y_1)}{m} + \frac{\hat\sigma_n^2(y_0)}{n-m}\right\}$. (5) $\mathrm{E}_X(\hat V_n^a - V_n) = (n-1)^{-1}\{\sigma_n^2(y_1) + \sigma_n^2(y_0) - 2\sigma_n(y_1, y_0)\} \ge 0$. (6) $\hat V_n^{b\pm} = \frac{1}{n-1}\left[\frac{n-m}{m}\hat\sigma_n^2(y_1) + \frac{m}{n-m}\hat\sigma_n^2(y_0) \pm 2\{\hat\sigma_n^2(y_1)\hat\sigma_n^2(y_0)\}^{1/2}\right]$. [Marginal distributions and sharp bounds: Section 3, p. 853 (PDF p. 4)] Let $G_N(y) = N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N I(y_{1i} \le y)$ and $F_N(y) = N^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N I(y_{0i} \le y)$ be the marginal distribution functions of $y_1$ and $y_0$, respectively. Define their left-continuous inverses as $G_N^{-1}(u) = \inf\{y : G_N(y) \ge u\}$ and $F_N^{-1}(u) = \inf\{y : F_N(y) \ge u\}$. Define also (7) $\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0) = \int_0^1 G_N^{-1}(u)F_N^{-1}(u)\,du - \mu_N(y_1)\mu_N(y_0)$, $\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0) = \int_0^1 G_N^{-1}(u)F_N^{-1}(1-u)\,du - \mu_N(y_1)\mu_N(y_0)$. [p. 853] $V_N^H = \frac{1}{N-1}\left\{\frac{N-m}{m}\sigma_N^2(y_1) + \frac{N-(n-m)}{n-m}\sigma_N^2(y_0) + 2\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0)\right\}$, $V_N^L = \frac{1}{N-1}\left\{\frac{N-m}{m}\sigma_N^2(y_1) + \frac{N-(n-m)}{n-m}\sigma_N^2(y_0) + 2\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0)\right\}$. [Estimators: p. 854 (PDF p. 5)] In practice, we observe neither $G_N$ nor $F_N$, but rather their estimates $\hat G_N(y) = m^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^T I(y_{1i} \le y)$, $\hat F_N(y) = (n-m)^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^N X_i^C I(y_{0i} \le y)$ and left-continuous inverses $\hat G_N^{-1}(u) = \inf\{y : \hat G_N(y) \ge u\} = y_{1(\lceil mu\rceil)}$, $\hat F_N^{-1}(u) = \inf\{y : \hat F_N(y) \ge u\} = y_{0(m+\lceil (n-m)u\rceil)}$, where $y_{1(1)} \le \cdots \le y_{1(m)}$ and $y_{0(m+1)} \le \cdots \le y_{0(n)}$ are the ordered observed outcomes, and $\lceil x\rceil$ denotes the smallest integer greater than or equal to $x$. Substituting $(\hat G_N, \hat F_N)$ for $(G_N, F_N)$ in (7) yields an interval estimator $[\hat\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0), \hat\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0)]$ for $\sigma_N(y_1, y_0)$: $\hat\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0) = \int_0^1 \hat G_N^{-1}(u)\hat F_N^{-1}(u)\,du - \hat\mu_N(y_1)\hat\mu_N(y_0)$, $\hat\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0) = \int_0^1 \hat G_N^{-1}(u)\hat F_N^{-1}(1-u)\,du - \hat\mu_N(y_1)\hat\mu_N(y_0)$. Let the $[0, 1]$-partition $\mathcal{P}_{m,n} = \{p_0, p_1, \ldots, p_P\}$ be the ordered distinct elements of $\{0, 1/m, 2/m, \ldots, 1\} \cup \{0, 1/(n-m), 2/(n-m), \ldots, 1\}$. Let $y_{1[i]} = y_{1(\lceil mp_i\rceil)}$ and $y_{0[i]} = y_{0\{m+\lceil (n-m)p_i\rceil\}}$. The inverses $\hat G_N^{-1}$ and $\hat F_N^{-1}$ are piecewise constant since $\hat G_N^{-1}(u) = y_{1[i]}$ and $\hat F_N^{-1}(u) = y_{0[i]}$ for $u \in (p_{i-1}, p_i]$. In addition, the symmetry $p_i = 1 - p_{P-i}$ implies that $p_i - p_{i-1} = p_{P+1-i} - p_{P-i}$. Thus, $[\hat\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0), \hat\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0)]$ reduces to (8) $\hat\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0) = \sum_{i=1}^P (p_i - p_{i-1})y_{1[i]}y_{0[i]} - \hat\mu_N(y_1)\hat\mu_N(y_0)$, $\hat\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0) = \sum_{i=1}^P (p_i - p_{i-1})y_{1[i]}y_{0[P+1-i]} - \hat\mu_N(y_1)\hat\mu_N(y_0)$, where $\hat\mu_N(y_1)$ and $\hat\mu_N(y_0)$ are as defined in (1). Substituting $\hat\sigma_N^2(y_1)$, $\hat\sigma_N^2(y_0)$, and (8) for $\{\sigma_N^2(y_1), \sigma_N^2(y_0), \sigma_N(y_1, y_0)\}$ in the expressions for $V_N^L$ and $V_N^H$, we obtain the interval estimator $[\hat V_N^L, \hat V_N^H]$ for $V_N$: (9) $\hat V_N^H = \frac{1}{N-1}\left\{\frac{N-m}{m}\hat\sigma_N^2(y_1) + \frac{N-(n-m)}{n-m}\hat\sigma_N^2(y_0) + 2\hat\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0)\right\}$, $\hat V_N^L = \frac{1}{N-1}\left\{\frac{N-m}{m}\hat\sigma_N^2(y_1) + \frac{N-(n-m)}{n-m}\hat\sigma_N^2(y_0) + 2\hat\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0)\right\}$. [Asymptotic setting: Section 4, p. 855 (PDF p. 6)] Let $\{U_N\}_N$ be a nested sequence of finite populations. The potential outcomes $y_1$ and $y_0$ of each unit are fixed, and hence the population grows deterministically. As in Isaki and Fuller [10], we do not assume that the sequences of treatment assignments are nested; instead, each $U_N$ hosts its own random assignment. Let $H_N(\cdot, \cdot)$ be the joint distribution function of $(y_1, y_0)$ for $U_N$. [Conditions of Proposition 1, p. 855 (PDF p. 6), 'as $N \to \infty$'] 1. $(m/N, n/N) \to (\theta\rho, \theta)$ for $\theta \in (0, 1]$ and $\rho \in (0, 1)$; 2. $H_N$ converges weakly to a limit distribution $H$ with marginals $G(y) = H(y, \infty)$ and $F(y) = H(\infty, y)$; 3. $G_N(y) \to G(y)$ at any discontinuity point of $G$, and $F_N(y) \to F(y)$ at any discontinuity point of $F$; 4. The sequences of distributions represented by $\{G_N\}_N$ and $\{F_N\}_N$ are uniformly square-integrable. That is, as $\beta \to \infty$, $\sup_N\left\{\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i : y_{1i}^2 \ge \beta} y_{1i}^2\right\}$, $\sup_N\left\{\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i : y_{0i}^2 \ge \beta} y_{0i}^2\right\} \to 0$.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Equation (11) in the proof of Lemma 2, corrected (with equation (12))
canonical_claim.statement: [Printed: p. 861 (PDF p. 12)] Noting that $\sigma_N^2(I\{y_1 \le y\}) = G_N(y)\{1 - G_N(y)\} \le 1/4$ and similarly $\sigma_N^2(I\{y_0 \le y\}) \le 1/4$, we have for all $y$, (11) $\mathrm{Var}_X\hat G_N(y) = \frac{N-m}{(N-1)m}\sigma_N^2\left(I\{y_1 \le y\}\right) = \frac{N-m}{4(N-1)m}$, (12) $\mathrm{Var}_X\hat F_N(y) = \frac{N-(n-m)}{(N-1)(n-m)}\sigma_N^2\left(I\{y_0 \le y\}\right) \le \frac{N-(n-m)}{4(N-1)(n-m)}$. [Corrected statement: the last relation of (11) is an inequality, as in (12).] For all $y$, (11) $\mathrm{Var}_X\hat G_N(y) = \frac{N-m}{(N-1)m}\sigma_N^2\left(I\{y_1 \le y\}\right) = \frac{N-m}{(N-1)m}G_N(y)\{1 - G_N(y)\} \le \frac{N-m}{4(N-1)m}$, and (12) as printed, with $\sigma_N^2\left(I\{y_0 \le y\}\right) = F_N(y)\{1 - F_N(y)\}$. Also $\mathrm{E}_X\hat G_N(y) = G_N(y)$ and $\mathrm{E}_X\hat F_N(y) = F_N(y)$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The population, the design, $\mu_N$, $\sigma_N^2$, $\sigma_N(\cdot,\cdot)$, $\tau_N$, $\hat\tau_N$, $\mathrm{E}_X$, $V_N$ of (2), $\hat\sigma_N^2$, $G_N$, $F_N$ and their left-continuous inverses, (7), $V_N^H$, $V_N^L$, $\hat G_N$, $\hat F_N$, the partition $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$, (8), (9), and for $n = N$ (3), (4), (6) are transcribed in the standing assumptions, with locations. $\sigma_N^2(I\{y_1 \le y\})$ is the finite population variance of the $N$ indicators $I(y_{1i} \le y)$, $i = 1, \ldots, N$; $\mathrm{Var}_X$ is the variance over the $\binom{N}{n}\binom{n}{m}$ equally likely assignments. [p. 861 (PDF p. 12), after (10)] $\mathrm{E}_X\hat G_N(y) = G_N(y)$. [p. 861] The argument used to derive (2) can also be used to bound the variances in (10).
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: The statement is exact for each $N$, $n$, $m$ and each real $y$. Steps: marginally the treatment group is a uniformly random $m$-subset of $U_N$ and the control group a uniformly random $(n-m)$-subset; for values $v_1, \ldots, v_N$ and a uniformly random $k$-subset $S$, $\mathrm{E}\left(\frac1k\sum_{i \in S}v_i\right) = \mu_N(v)$ and $\mathrm{Var}\left(\frac1k\sum_{i \in S}v_i\right) = \frac{N-k}{(N-1)k}\sigma_N^2(v)$; for $v_i \in \{0, 1\}$ with mean $g$, $\sigma_N^2(v) = g(1-g) \le 1/4$. The same identities hold for the indicators $I(y_{1i} < y)$, that is for $\hat G_N(y-)$, which is what the corrected Lemma 2 (P022-T2) uses at the points $s_i-$.
canonical_claim.note: P022-E005 is rated an error, Minor: a misprinted relation in an identity ('=' printed where '$\le$' is meant; the sentence before (11) and the companion display (12) have the bound). Sol's smallest repair (validated.json): $\mathrm{Var}_X\hat G_N(y) = \frac{N-m}{(N-1)m}G_N(y)\{1 - G_N(y)\} \le \frac{N-m}{4(N-1)m}$. The proof of Lemma 2 uses only the upper bound, in (10). Equations (11)–(12) lie in the proof of Lemma 2, which serves headline claims P022-H1 and P022-H6; the rating records no headline claim as affected. The corrected (11)–(12) are also the variance input of P022-T2 and P022-T3.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Equation (11) in the proof of Lemma 2, as printed
canonical_claim.statement: [Printed relation refuted: p. 861 (PDF p. 12)] we have for all $y$, (11) $\mathrm{Var}_X\hat G_N(y) = \frac{N-m}{(N-1)m}\sigma_N^2\left(I\{y_1 \le y\}\right) = \frac{N-m}{4(N-1)m}$. [Counterexample, from the validator] $N = n = 4$, $m = 2$, and a threshold $y$ below every treatment potential outcome; for instance $y_{1i} = y_{0i} = 1$ for $i = 1, \ldots, 4$ and $y = 0$. Then $I(y_{1i} \le y) = 0$ for every $i$, so $G_N(y) = 0$ and $\sigma_N^2(I\{y_1 \le y\}) = 0$; $\hat G_N(y) = 0$ for each of the $\binom{4}{2} = 6$ assignments, so $\mathrm{Var}_X\hat G_N(y) = 0$. The printed last member is $\frac{N-m}{4(N-1)m} = \frac{2}{4 \cdot 3 \cdot 2} = \frac{1}{12} \ne 0$. In general, for $m < N$ the last relation of (11) holds with equality if and only if $G_N(y) = 1/2$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The population, the design, $\mu_N$, $\sigma_N^2$, $\sigma_N(\cdot,\cdot)$, $\tau_N$, $\hat\tau_N$, $\mathrm{E}_X$, $V_N$ of (2), $\hat\sigma_N^2$, $G_N$, $F_N$ and their left-continuous inverses, (7), $V_N^H$, $V_N^L$, $\hat G_N$, $\hat F_N$, the partition $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$, (8), (9), and for $n = N$ (3), (4), (6) are transcribed in the standing assumptions, with locations. $\sigma_N^2(I\{y_1 \le y\})$ is the finite population variance of the $N$ indicators $I(y_{1i} \le y)$, $i = 1, \ldots, N$; $\mathrm{Var}_X$ is the variance over the $\binom{N}{n}\binom{n}{m}$ equally likely assignments. [p. 861 (PDF p. 12), after (10)] $\mathrm{E}_X\hat G_N(y) = G_N(y)$. [p. 861] The argument used to derive (2) can also be used to bound the variances in (10).
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: A finite check over the six assignments of two of four units to treatment. The first equality of (11) holds in the instance (both sides are $0$); only the last relation fails. $g(1-g) = 1/4$ if and only if $g = 1/2$.
canonical_claim.note: From the batch validator's derivation (validate/_batch/P022-B01/work/derivations.md, under E005): 'For N=4, m=2 and a threshold below every treatment potential, all six sampled CDFs equal zero, giving Var=0, whereas the printed final expression is 1/12.' The explicit outcome values are one such instance; the setting of p. 851 ($N \ge 4$, $m \ge 2$, $n - m \ge 2$) is met. The corrected relation is P022-T4.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Appendix B, function sharp.var: partition points and integration weights, corrected
canonical_claim.location: p. 869 (PDF p. 20); equations (8)–(9) on p. 854 (PDF p. 5)
canonical_claim.statement: [Printed claim: Appendix B, p. 869 (PDF p. 20)] Here, we present R code for the function sharp.var, which outputs the bound estimates $\hat V_N^H$ (given input upper=TRUE) and $\hat V_N^L$ (given input upper=FALSE). The other inputs are yt (the observed outcomes under treatment), yc (the observed outcomes under control) and N (the total number of units in the population). [Printed lines corrected, p. 869] The lines of sharp.var that set p_i (the subtraction of .Machine\$double.eps^.5 from every partition point and the resetting of p_i[1] to .Machine\$double.eps^.5), the selections yti and yci made at those points, and the weights (p_i-p_i_minus) in the returned expression; the routine is transcribed in full in P022-T9. [Corrected claim, from Sol's smallest repair] Keep the partition $0 = p_0 < p_1 < \cdots < p_P = 1$ of (8) and its widths $p_r - p_{r-1}$, and use the cell midpoints $u_r = (p_{r-1} + p_r)/2$ only to select the empirical quantiles. With $k = n - m$, $a_1 \le \cdots \le a_m$ the sorted treatment outcomes, $b_1 \le \cdots \le b_k$ the sorted control outcomes, $\bar y_t$, $\bar y_c$ their means, $Q_t(u) = a_{\lceil mu\rceil}$, $Q_c^H(u) = b_{\lceil ku\rceil}$ and $Q_c^L(u) = b_{k+1-\lceil ku\rceil}$, the routine computes $\hat\sigma_N^B = \sum_{r=1}^P(p_r - p_{r-1})\{Q_t(u_r) - \bar y_t\}\{Q_c^B(u_r) - \bar y_c\}$ for $B \in \{H, L\}$ and substitutes it, with the unchanged marginal variance terms, into (9). [Formal content] For all real outcomes, with $m \ge 2$ and $k \ge 2$: (a) for every $r$ and every $u \in (p_{r-1}, p_r)$: $\lceil mu\rceil = \lceil mp_r\rceil$, $\lceil ku\rceil = \lceil kp_r\rceil$ and $k + 1 - \lceil ku\rceil = \lceil kp_{P+1-r}\rceil$; (b) $\sum_{r=1}^P(p_r - p_{r-1}) = 1$, $\sum_{r=1}^P(p_r - p_{r-1})Q_t(u_r) = \bar y_t$ and $\sum_{r=1}^P(p_r - p_{r-1})Q_c^B(u_r) = \bar y_c$ for $B \in \{H, L\}$; (c) hence $\sum_{r=1}^P(p_r - p_{r-1})\{Q_t(u_r) - \bar y_t\}\{Q_c^H(u_r) - \bar y_c\} = \sum_{i=1}^P(p_i - p_{i-1})y_{1[i]}y_{0[i]} - \hat\mu_N(y_1)\hat\mu_N(y_0)$ and $\sum_{r=1}^P(p_r - p_{r-1})\{Q_t(u_r) - \bar y_t\}\{Q_c^L(u_r) - \bar y_c\} = \sum_{i=1}^P(p_i - p_{i-1})y_{1[i]}y_{0[P+1-i]} - \hat\mu_N(y_1)\hat\mu_N(y_0)$: the corrected routine returns exactly $\hat V_N^H$ and $\hat V_N^L$ of (8)–(9); (d) equivalently, with $w_{ij} = \frac{[\min(ik, jm) - \max((i-1)k, (j-1)m)]_+}{mk}$ for $1 \le i \le m$, $1 \le j \le k$: $\sum_jw_{ij} = 1/m$, $\sum_iw_{ij} = 1/k$, $\hat\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0) = \sum_{i,j}w_{ij}(a_i - \bar y_t)(b_j - \bar y_c)$ and $\hat\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0) = \sum_{i,j}w_{ij}(a_i - \bar y_t)(b_{k+1-j} - \bar y_c)$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The population, the design, $\mu_N$, $\sigma_N^2$, $\sigma_N(\cdot,\cdot)$, $\tau_N$, $\hat\tau_N$, $\mathrm{E}_X$, $V_N$ of (2), $\hat\sigma_N^2$, $G_N$, $F_N$ and their left-continuous inverses, (7), $V_N^H$, $V_N^L$, $\hat G_N$, $\hat F_N$, the partition $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$, (8), (9), and for $n = N$ (3), (4), (6) are transcribed in the standing assumptions, with locations. In the notation of p. 854, $a_i = y_{1(i)}$, $b_j = y_{0(m+j)}$, $\bar y_t = \hat\mu_N(y_1)$, $\bar y_c = \hat\mu_N(y_0)$, $y_{1[i]} = a_{\lceil mp_i\rceil}$ and $y_{0[i]} = b_{\lceil kp_i\rceil}$. $[x]_+ = \max(x, 0)$. The full printed routine is transcribed in P022-T9.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (i) Every $i/m$ and every $j/k$ is a partition point, so no $mu$ or $ku$ is an integer for $u$ in the interior of a cell, and $(p_{r-1}, p_r] \subseteq ((i-1)/m, i/m]$ for $i = \lceil mp_r\rceil$ (likewise for $k$): this gives the first two equalities of (a). (ii) $\lceil k(1-u)\rceil = k - \lfloor ku\rfloor = k + 1 - \lceil ku\rceil$ when $ku$ is not an integer, and $1 - u \in (p_{P-r}, p_{P+1-r})$ by the symmetry $p_i = 1 - p_{P-i}$: the third equality of (a). (iii) The cells with $\lceil mp_r\rceil = i$ have total width $1/m$, those with $\lceil kp_r\rceil = j$ total width $1/k$: this gives (b). (iv) Expanding the centred product with (b) gives (c). (v) $w_{ij}$ is the length of $((i-1)/m, i/m] \cap ((j-1)/k, j/k]$, the total width of the cells with $\lceil mp_r\rceil = i$ and $\lceil kp_r\rceil = j$: this gives (d).
canonical_claim.note: P022-E002 is rated an error, Minor. It is a finding about the routine printed in Appendix B; it is a target because the routine is part of the published text, its defect is one of exact arithmetic (the integration weights are wrong; this is not floating-point noise) and the correction is a formula. Sol's smallest repair and the prior correction (validated.json): midpoint selection with the unaltered widths; centring is a numerical refinement that does not change the value in real arithmetic. Derivation: validate/P022-E002/v1/artifact/derivation.md, Section 6; the validator's repaired routine is validate/P022-E002/v1/artifact/repaired_code.R. Model the routine in real arithmetic; floating-point rounding is not part of the target. Two other findings about the same routine are not targets in their own right: P022-E004 (the line break before '*' in the definition of FPvar stops the printed code from parsing) is a typesetting defect with no mathematical statement to correct, and P022-E003 (N=Inf) is covered by P022-T10.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: Appendix B, function sharp.var, as printed
canonical_claim.location: p. 869 (PDF p. 20); equations (8)–(9) on p. 854 (PDF p. 5)
canonical_claim.statement:
[Printed claim: Appendix B, p. 869 (PDF p. 20)] Here, we present R code for the function sharp.var, which outputs the bound estimates $\hat V_N^H$ (given input upper=TRUE) and $\hat V_N^L$ (given input upper=FALSE). The other inputs are yt (the observed outcomes under treatment), yc (the observed outcomes under control) and N (the total number of units in the population). [Printed code, p. 869 (PDF p. 20), verbatim with its line breaks; the character \$ in .Machine\$double.eps is R syntax, written unescaped inside the code]
sharp.var <- function(yt,yc,N=length(c(yt,yc)),upper=TRUE) {
 m <- length(yt)
 n <- m + length(yc)
 FPvar <- function(x,N) (N-1)/(N*(length(x)-1))
   * sum((x - mean(x))^2)
 yt <- sort(yt)
 if(upper == TRUE) yc <- sort(yc) else
   yc <- sort(yc,decreasing=TRUE)
 p_i <- unique(sort(c(seq(0,n-m,1)/(n-m),seq(0,m,1)/m))) -
 .Machine$double.eps^.5
 p_i[1] <- .Machine$double.eps^.5
 yti <- yt[ceiling(p_i*m)]
 yci <- yc[ceiling(p_i*(n-m))]
 p_i_minus <- c(NA,p_i[1: (length(p_i)-1)])
 return(((N-m)/m * FPvar(yt,N) + (N-(n-m))/(n-m) * FPvar(yc,N)
   + 2*sum(((p_i-p_i_minus)*yti*yci)[2:length(p_i)])
   - 2*mean(yt)*mean(yc))/(N-1))
}
[Reading of the routine in real arithmetic] Write $k = n - m$, $a_1 \le \cdots \le a_m$ for the sorted treatment outcomes, $b_1 \le \cdots \le b_k$ for the sorted control outcomes, $\bar y_t$, $\bar y_c$ for their means, and $e = 2^{-26}$ for the value of .Machine\$double.eps^.5 (binary64 machine epsilon is $2^{-52}$). FPvar is read as the single expression $\frac{N-1}{N(\mathrm{length}(x)-1)}\sum(x - \bar x)^2$, so FPvar(yt,N) $= \hat\sigma_N^2(y_1)$ and FPvar(yc,N) $= \hat\sigma_N^2(y_0)$. With $0 = p_0 < p_1 < \cdots < p_P = 1$ the partition $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$ of (8), the routine forms the points $q_0 = e$ and $q_j = p_j - e$ for $1 \le j \le P$, selects $a_{\lceil mq_j\rceil}$ and, for upper=TRUE, $b_{\lceil kq_j\rceil}$ (for upper=FALSE, $b_{k+1-\lceil kq_j\rceil}$), and returns $V_{\mathrm{code}}^B = \frac{1}{N-1}\left\{\frac{N-m}{m}\hat\sigma_N^2(y_1) + \frac{N-(n-m)}{n-m}\hat\sigma_N^2(y_0) + 2\sum_{j=1}^P(q_j - q_{j-1})a_{\lceil mq_j\rceil}b^B_j - 2\bar y_t\bar y_c\right\}$, where $b^H_j = b_{\lceil kq_j\rceil}$ and $b^L_j = b_{k+1-\lceil kq_j\rceil}$. [Counterexample, from the validator] $N = n = 4$, $m = n - m = 2$, and $y_{1i} = y_{0i} = 1$ for $i = 1, \ldots, 4$. Each of the six assignments gives yt $= (1, 1)$ and yc $= (1, 1)$, and $\hat\tau_N = 0$ for each, so $V_N = 0$. By (8)–(9): $\hat\sigma_N^2(y_1) = \hat\sigma_N^2(y_0) = 0$, the partition is $(0, 1/2, 1)$, $\hat\sigma_N^H(y_1, y_0) = \hat\sigma_N^L(y_1, y_0) = \frac12 \cdot 1 + \frac12 \cdot 1 - 1 \cdot 1 = 0$, and $\hat V_N^H = \hat V_N^L = 0$. The routine: $(q_0, q_1, q_2) = (e, \frac12 - e, 1 - e)$; the selected values are all $1$; the weights are $q_1 - q_0 = \frac12 - 2e$ and $q_2 - q_1 = \frac12$, with sum $1 - 2e = \frac{33554431}{33554432}$; so $V_{\mathrm{code}}^H = V_{\mathrm{code}}^L = \frac{0 + 0 + 2(1 - 2e) - 2}{3} = -\frac{4e}{3} = -\frac{1}{50331648}$. The routine does not output $\hat V_N^H = \hat V_N^L = 0$, and its output is negative. [General identity, from the validator] In real arithmetic, whenever every width $p_j - p_{j-1}$ exceeds $2e$: $\sum_{j=1}^P(q_j - q_{j-1}) = 1 - 2e$, $V_{\mathrm{code}}^H - \hat V_N^H = -\frac{4e\,a_1b_1}{N-1}$ and $V_{\mathrm{code}}^L - \hat V_N^L = -\frac{4e\,a_1b_k}{N-1}$, where $a_1 = \min(\mathrm{yt})$, $b_1 = \min(\mathrm{yc})$ and $b_k = \max(\mathrm{yc})$. In particular the output changes when the same constant is added to every outcome, which $\hat V_N^H$ and $\hat V_N^L$ do not.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The population, the design, $\mu_N$, $\sigma_N^2$, $\sigma_N(\cdot,\cdot)$, $\tau_N$, $\hat\tau_N$, $\mathrm{E}_X$, $V_N$ of (2), $\hat\sigma_N^2$, $G_N$, $F_N$ and their left-continuous inverses, (7), $V_N^H$, $V_N^L$, $\hat G_N$, $\hat F_N$, the partition $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$, (8), (9), and for $n = N$ (3), (4), (6) are transcribed in the standing assumptions, with locations. In the notation of p. 854, $a_i = y_{1(i)}$, $b_j = y_{0(m+j)}$, $\bar y_t = \hat\mu_N(y_1)$, $\bar y_c = \hat\mu_N(y_0)$. In R, p_i has entries $q_0, \ldots, q_P$ at positions $1, \ldots, P+1$; p_i_minus is p_i shifted by one position with NA first; the subscript [2:length(p_i)] keeps the terms $j = 1, \ldots, P$; sort(yc,decreasing=TRUE) reverses the control order, so that position $\lceil kq_j\rceil$ of the reversed vector is $b_{k+1-\lceil kq_j\rceil}$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: (i) If $p_j - p_{j-1} > 2e$ for all $j$, then $q_j = p_j - e \in (p_{j-1}, p_j)$ for $1 \le j \le P$, so $\lceil mq_j\rceil = \lceil mp_j\rceil$ and $\lceil kq_j\rceil = \lceil kp_j\rceil$ (P022-T8 (a)): the selected values are those of (8). (ii) $q_1 - q_0 = (p_1 - p_0) - 2e > 0$ and $q_j - q_{j-1} = p_j - p_{j-1}$ for $j \ge 2$: only the first weight differs, by $-2e$. (iii) The first selected product is $a_1b_1$ for upper=TRUE and $a_1b_k$ for upper=FALSE; the factor $2/(N-1)$ in the returned expression gives the two differences. (iv) In the instance: $\lceil 2e\rceil = 1$, $\lceil 2(\frac12 - e)\rceil = 1$, $\lceil 2(1 - e)\rceil = 2$; $4e/3 = 4/(3 \cdot 2^{26}) = 1/50331648$.
canonical_claim.note: From validate/P022-E002/v1/artifact/derivation.md, Sections 2–5 (exact rational check in exact_check.py and exact_output.txt; native R output in native_output.txt, which returns the rounded value $-1.9868214925130207 \times 10^{-8}$ for both modes). The defect is present in exact arithmetic with $e$ fixed at its machine value; it is not produced by rounding. The identity for the general case is asserted only when every cell is wider than $2e$ (for narrower cells the shifted points can change ranks); in the application ($m = 781$, $n - m = 780$) the cells are at least $1/609180$ wide. The printed line break inside FPvar (P022-E004) is joined in the reading. No published number is shown to change: the bound on the discrepancy for the application is $4e \cdot 150^2/1560 \approx 8.6 \times 10^{-7}$ USD$^2$. The corrected routine is P022-T8.

canonical_claim.name_in_paper: The infinite-population case ($N = \infty$) of the estimator: Introduction and Section 2, and Appendix B called with N=Inf, corrected claim
canonical_claim.location: p. 850 (PDF p. 1); p. 852 (PDF p. 3); Appendix B, p. 869 (PDF p. 20)
canonical_claim.statement: [Printed: p. 850 (PDF p. 1)] Our estimator is also applicable to all possible cases of $N$ and $n$ ($n = N < \infty$, $n < N < \infty$, and $N = \infty$), thus providing a unified treatment of the problem. […] When the population size $N$ is infinite, our estimator recovers the standard variance point estimator for mean differences between independent groups [13]. [p. 852 (PDF p. 3)] However, when the population being sampled from is infinite ($N = \infty$), Neyman [13] noted that the control and treatment units are effectively sampled independently from their respective distributions. Hence, the covariance term vanishes, and $V_N$ is point identified. To see this, let $N \to \infty$ while holding $m$ and $n$ fixed so that $V_N \to \frac{1}{m}\sigma_N^2(y_1) + \frac{1}{n-m}\sigma_N^2(y_0)$, the sampling variance for the difference of independent means. [p. 869 (PDF p. 20)] […] the function sharp.var, which outputs the bound estimates $\hat V_N^H$ (given input upper=TRUE) and $\hat V_N^L$ (given input upper=FALSE). The other inputs are […] N (the total number of units in the population). [Finding] Called with N=Inf, the printed routine evaluates (N-1)/(N*(length(x)-1)) as Inf/Inf and returns NaN for both values of upper. [Corrected claim, from Sol's smallest repair] In sharp.var, immediately after m and n are defined, insert: if (is.infinite(N) && N > 0) return(stats::var(yt)/m + stats::var(yc)/(n-m)). This returns the limit of the estimator, in either mode. [Formal content] (a) [The estimator.] Fix the observed outcomes ($m \ge 2$ treated, $n - m \ge 2$ control) and let $s_1^2 = \frac{1}{m-1}\sum_{i=1}^m\{y_{1i} - \hat\mu_N(y_1)\}^2$ and $s_0^2 = \frac{1}{n-m-1}\sum_{i=m+1}^n\{y_{0i} - \hat\mu_N(y_0)\}^2$. For every $N \ge n$ and $B \in \{H, L\}$, with $\hat\sigma_N^B(y_1, y_0)$ of (8), which does not depend on $N$: $\hat V_N^B = \left(\frac1m - \frac1N\right)s_1^2 + \left(\frac{1}{n-m} - \frac1N\right)s_0^2 + \frac{2\hat\sigma_N^B(y_1, y_0)}{N-1}$. Hence $\lim_{N \to \infty}\hat V_N^H = \lim_{N \to \infty}\hat V_N^L = \frac{s_1^2}{m} + \frac{s_0^2}{n-m}$, the value returned by the corrected branch. (b) [The variance, p. 852.] For every $N$: $V_N - \left\{\frac1m\sigma_N^2(y_1) + \frac{1}{n-m}\sigma_N^2(y_0)\right\} = \frac{1}{N-1}\left\{2\sigma_N(y_1, y_0) - \left(1 - \frac1m\right)\sigma_N^2(y_1) - \left(1 - \frac{1}{n-m}\right)\sigma_N^2(y_0)\right\}$, which tends to $0$ as $N \to \infty$ with $m$ and $n$ fixed whenever $\sigma_N^2(y_1)$ and $\sigma_N^2(y_0)$ stay bounded. [Instance, from the validator] yt $=$ yc $= (0, 1)$: $\hat V_N^H = \frac{N-2}{2N} + \frac{1}{2(N-1)}$ and $\hat V_N^L = \frac{N-2}{2N} - \frac{1}{2(N-1)}$ (so $5/12$ and $1/12$ at $N = 4$, $41/90$ and $31/90$ at $N = 10$); both tend to $1/2 = s_1^2/2 + s_0^2/2$.
canonical_claim.definitions_needed: The population, the design, $\mu_N$, $\sigma_N^2$, $\sigma_N(\cdot,\cdot)$, $\tau_N$, $\hat\tau_N$, $\mathrm{E}_X$, $V_N$ of (2), $\hat\sigma_N^2$, $G_N$, $F_N$ and their left-continuous inverses, (7), $V_N^H$, $V_N^L$, $\hat G_N$, $\hat F_N$, the partition $\mathcal{P}_{m,n}$, (8), (9), and for $n = N$ (3), (4), (6) are transcribed in the standing assumptions, with locations. stats::var is the sample variance with divisor one less than the sample size, so stats::var(yt) $= s_1^2$ and stats::var(yc) $= s_0^2$; $\hat\sigma_N^2(y_1) = \frac{N-1}{N}s_1^2$ and $\hat\sigma_N^2(y_0) = \frac{N-1}{N}s_0^2$. 'The standard variance point estimator for mean differences between independent groups' is $s_1^2/m + s_0^2/(n-m)$.
canonical_claim.finite_lemmas: Exact for each $N \ge n$: $\frac{1}{N-1}\cdot\frac{N-m}{m}\cdot\frac{N-1}{N} = \frac1m - \frac1N$ and $\frac{1}{N-1}\cdot\frac{N-(n-m)}{n-m}\cdot\frac{N-1}{N} = \frac{1}{n-m} - \frac1N$, which give the displayed expression for $\hat V_N^B$ from (9); $\hat\sigma_N^B(y_1, y_0)$ in (8) is a function of the observed outcomes, $m$ and $n$ only. For (b): $\frac{N-m}{(N-1)m} - \frac1m = -\frac{1}{N-1}\left(1 - \frac1m\right)$, the same with $n - m$, and $|\sigma_N(y_1, y_0)| \le \{\sigma_N^2(y_1)\sigma_N^2(y_0)\}^{1/2}$.
canonical_claim.note: P022-E003 is rated an error, Minor (verdict confirmed in part). It is a finding about the printed routine: the paper's statements about the infinite-population limit are correct and no printed formula changes. It is a target because the whole content of the correction is the limit identity (a), which is also the mathematical part of headline claim P022-H4 (the estimator 'recovers the standard variance point estimator' when $N = \infty$); no separate headline target is listed for P022-H4. The NaN produced by floating-point evaluation of Inf/Inf is not a mathematical statement and is not to be formalized. Derivation: validate/P022-E003/v1/artifact/derivation.md (steps 2–5 and 9). Part (b) is the paper's own justification on p. 852, read with marginal variances that stay bounded as $N$ grows (P022-A002, which asked for an explicit moment condition, is rated not confirmed; the identity is from validate/_batch/P022-B01/work/derivations.md, under A002). The other part of P022-H4, that for dichotomous outcomes and $n = N$ the estimator 'essentially reproduces the estimator proposed by Robins [14], equation (3), with a slight difference due to finite population corrections' (p. 855), is not a target: Robins's formula is not in the paper and was not obtained (P022-N001, not confirmed).
